instruction:
OpenRouterBatchBackend throws away the provider's explanation when a batch is rejected. The batch object returned by GET <base>/batches/<id> carries it as {"error": {"message": "HTTP 400: invalid batch inference job: job-submission-count for account alex-79b5d6, in use: 16, quota: 16"}}, but status() normalizes only the status string, so a run whose batch the provider rejected reports every card as failed with no reason at all and the operator has to curl the API by hand to find out why.

Add a public method failure_reason(batch_id) to OpenRouterBatchBackend that performs one _retrieve and returns the provider's error message as a string, or None when the batch object carries no error message. Reuse _retrieve so the read-after-write grace window keeps working, and return None -- never raise -- when the batch is not visible yet (_BatchNotVisibleYet). Leave the behaviour of every existing public method exactly as it is.

Also write a NEW self-contained pytest file tests/test_batch_failure_reason.py covering: the message is returned for a rejected batch, None for a batch object with no error, and None when the batch is not visible yet. Drive it through the constructor's transport=... seam the same way tests/test_batch_backends.py does, but define your own fakes inside the new file -- do not import from another test module.
